parties:
Nizam Sheikh and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Alauddin Sheikh and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 6. On a perusal of the decision reported in 33 DLR(AD)113, it appears that the self-same question came up for consideration before the Appellate Division wherein it has been held that on account of omission of necessary party a pre-emption case shall not be dismissed out right keeping in view the provision of Order 1, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, inasmuch as, non-joinder of necessary party will not be itself defeat a suit proceeding. However, the special statutory provision in sub-section (2) as to the necessary parties to be impleaded as mandatory. In clear language it mentions the persons to be impleaded in an application made under sub-section (1) by a co-sharer tenant; and in an application made by a tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred. Requirement of the statutory provision cannot be minimised by the procedural law as contained in Order 1, rule 9. The special provision in sub-section (2) is not controlled by Order 1, rule 9, which merely provides that a suit shall not be dismissed by reason of mere non-joinder of necessary parties. Order 1, rule 10 provides for addition of party at any stage of the proceedings, either upon or without the application of either party. Where there is non-joinder of a necessary party the Court is empowered to add the necessary party under rule 10 at any stage of the proceedings either upon or without the application of either party. The objection as to non-joinder of necessary parties must be taken at the earliest opportunity by the defendant. Such objection provides an opportunity to the plaintiff to remove the defeat by adding parties who were omitted. In taking objection on the ground of non-joinder of necessary parties the defendant is required to furnish the names and particulars of the parties who were omitted from the suit and on the refusal of the plaintiff to implead the parties mentioned in the written statement, the question becomes an issue for adjudication by the court and on adjudication the question becomes decided. In such an event the consequence must follow, that is, the suit becomes liable to be dismissed on the ground of non-joinder of necessary party. In the case of a pre-emption proceeding the law regarding procedure cannot be treated as different. If the pre-emptee or for that matter any of the parties disclose existence of a necessary party and furnishes the necessary particulars, but the pre-emptor still in sits not to implead him as a party, consequence on adjudication is the same. Thus it appears that in a pre-emption proceeding the necessary parties may be added at any point of time after the institution of the suit but before the hearing of the same. It is now well settled that once an amendment is made the amendment will relate back to the date of institution of the pre-emption case as has been decided by the Appellate Division in 1986 BLD(AD)221. In that view of the matter the case reported in 14 DLR is no more a good law. Hence I do not find any substance in this revisional application. Thus it is summarily rejected.
